claims.feature: other: vague connection instead of predication
claims.claim: It states that rather than stating a relationship directly, LLMs allude vaguely to two subjects being connected to or associated with each other.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'
claims.quote: LLMs will often allude vaguely to the two subjects being
claims.page: section 'Vague expression of connection or association'

claims.claim: The guide reports a study documenting an over 10% decrease in the use of the words 'is' and 'are' in academic writing in 2023, with no major change in their frequency before that.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing', citing a study
claims.quote: documented an over 10% decrease in the usage of the words

claims.claim: The guide states that LLM output uses em dashes more often than nonprofessional human writing of the same genre.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'
claims.quote: LLM output uses them more often than nonprofessional human-written text

claims.claim: It adds that AI-generated em dashes are usually surrounded by spaces, contrary to typographic guidelines.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'
claims.quote: AI-generated em dashes are usually surrounded by spaces

claims.claim: The guide states that ChatGPT and DeepSeek typically produce curly quotation marks and curly apostrophes rather than straight ones, while Gemini and Claude models typically do not.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'
claims.quote: models typically do not use curly quotes

claims.claim: The guide states that LLMs overuse the rule of three, in forms from three stacked adjectives to three stacked short phrases, and use it to make superficial analysis look comprehensive.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, 'Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing'

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs will often allude vaguely to the two subjects being
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext fetched via ?action=raw (HTTP 200, 220246 bytes). Section 'Vague expression of connection or association' opens by contrasting directly stating a connection or relationship between two subjects with the vague alternative, and gives 'connected to' / 'associated with' as the examples. Every limb of the claim (direct statement avoided; vague allusion; the two connection/association wordings) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: documented an over 10% decrease in the usage of the words
verdicts.note: Section 'Avoidance of basic copulatives ("is"/"are" phrases)' attributes the figure to one study, names the two copulas, dates it to academic writing in 2023, and adds the no-major-change-before-that limb. Cited on the page to Geng and Trotta, 'Is ChatGPT Transforming Academics' Writing Style?' (arXiv 2404.08627). All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: LLM output uses them more often than nonprofessional human-written text
verdicts.note: Section 'Overuse of em dashes'. The sentence continues with the same-genre qualifier, so the claim's 'of the same genre' limb is supported too. Page attributes to the Washington Post and Kriss references.

verdicts.trueWording: AI-generated em dashes are usually surrounded by spaces
verdicts.note: Same section 'Overuse of em dashes', closing sentence of that paragraph. The page says 'contrary to common typographic guidelines'; the claim drops 'common', which narrows nothing material, so the second limb is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Gemini and Claude models typically do not use curly quotes
verdicts.note: Section 'Curly quotation marks and apostrophes'. Its first paragraph carries the ChatGPT/DeepSeek limb for both curly quotation marks (instead of straight) and the curly apostrophe (instead of the straight apostrophe); the Gemini/Claude exception, from which the claim's quote is drawn verbatim, sits three paragraphs later after the caveats about Chicago style, Word smart quotes and macOS.

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs overuse the rule of three
verdicts.note: Claim carried no quote to match, so graded on substance. Section 'Rule of three' states the overuse, then gives the range of forms as running from three repeated adjectives to three repeated short phrases, and closes by saying LLMs use the structure to make superficial analyses appear more comprehensive. All three limbs supported; wording differs from the claim's paraphrase 'three stacked'.
